title: ARE YOU DATING… OR JUST ENTERTAINING LONELINESS?
paragraphs: ARE YOU DATING… OR JUST ENTERTAINING LONELINESS?
The question doesn’t sound dangerous at first.
But sit with it long enough… and it starts to expose things you’ve been avoiding.
Because some relationships aren’t built on love.
On the fear of eating alone.
On nights that feel too long.
On the quiet panic that maybe… just maybe… no one else is coming.
Even when you know they don’t lead you closer to God.
Even when your spirit feels heavier after every conversation.
Even when deep down, something inside you whispers, “This isn’t it.”
But loneliness has a way of making almost anything feel like provision.
And suddenly, you’re not dating for purpose…
Scripture doesn’t ignore this kind of struggle.

“לֹא־טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָאָדָם לְבַדּוֹ”
Lo tov heyot ha’adam levado
“It is not good for man to be alone.”
But notice what God does next.
He doesn’t rush Adam into the nearest available connection.

“עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ”
Ezer kenegdo — a helper fit, corresponding, aligned.
And this is where many hearts quietly break.
You can be talking every day…
And still be completely outside God’s design.
And loneliness will lie to you if you let it.
“The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.”
We run into conversations we shouldn’t entertain.
We run into situationships we know won’t last.
We run into emotional attachments that slowly pull us away from obedience.
But what if the silence you’re trying to escape…
Is actually where God is trying to speak?
In the Greek of Matthew 6:33, Jesus says:

“ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν”
zēteite de prōton tēn basileian
Because anything you place before God…
Some of you aren’t in love.
To hearing your phone light up.
To knowing someone is thinking about you.
Even if they’re not leading you to Christ.
Even if they’re slowly pulling you away.
Even if your spirit feels quieter… weaker… more compromised.
And Jesus didn’t die so you could survive emotionally.
He died so you could be transformed completely.

“ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ, καινὴ κτίσις”
hōste ei tis en Christō, kainē ktisis
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.”
But new things require letting go of old patterns.
Yes… even the ones that feel good.
Because not everything that feels good is sent by God.
Some things feel good because they temporarily numb what God is trying to heal.
So let me ask you again…
The other leads to slow spiritual compromise.
And you already know which one you’re in.
You felt it while reading this.
That moment where you paused and thought…
Jesus doesn’t expose you to shame you.
He exposes you to free you.
And freedom sometimes starts with a hard decision:
Let your voice be heard. Someone else needs to see they’re not alone in this.
And if you know someone who’s been stuck in this cycle…
Follow closely if you want daily truth that doesn’t just comfort you—but transforms you.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Christ, about healing the parts of you that keep running back to what breaks you…
If you truly desire to glorify God, supporting what spreads His truth matters more than you think.
Because the same God who is calling you out of loneliness…
Is calling you into something far greater.
This exact moment you’re reading this…
Might be where everything begins to change.
You were never meant to be completed by attention…
You were meant to be transformed by Christ.
